negative_findings.description: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia, a.s., pobočka zahraničnej banky (IČO 47251336) has no Slovak-language investor-relations or annual-report page of its own; Slovak searches returned only register aggregators (registeruz, FinStat, D&B) and Wikipedia, not a bank-hosted výročná správa.
negative_findings.result_summary: Branch-level SK disclosure appears to route entirely through the Czech parent's výroční zpráva plus the Slovak RÚZ filing. No SK IR page located in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: UniCredit's Slovak technology decisions are made and disclosed in Prague/Milan, so any vendor-mention mining must target Czech- and Italian-language parent documents rather than SK sources — a language dimension outside this run's sk/en scope.

negative_findings.description: No standalone ČSOB Slovensko Pillar 3 / 'zverejňovanie informácií podľa Opatrenia NBS 16/2014' document was located in this pass — only the combined bilingual výročná správa PDFs from the /documents/11005/98584/ library.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search returned annual reports for 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2025 but no separate Pillar 3 file; the disclosures may be embedded in the annual report or on an unindexed sub-page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Pillar 3 operational-risk sections are where outsourcing dependencies surface most explicitly; if ČSOB embeds rather than separates them, the collector must parse whole annual reports instead of a small targeted document.

negative_findings.description: The only NBS 'Pilier III – výkazníctvo a zverejňovanie' page surfaced sits under the insurance (poisťovníctvo) supervision branch, not banking. The banking-sector disclosure-framework page on nbs.sk was not located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Slovak regulatory-term searches repeatedly returned the insurance Pillar III page as the top nbs.sk hit for both VÚB and Prima banka queries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without the banking-sector NBS page the collection calendar for bank disclosure documents (cadence, mandatory templates, outsourcing-notification duties) rests on inference from bank documents rather than on the supervisor's own statement.

negative_findings.description: Named technology vendors were NOT found inside the Slovak banks' own annual reports in this pass. The two concrete vendor attributions obtained (Temenos payment hub at Tatra banka; PosAm end-user-services outsourcing at Tatra banka) both came from vendor-side marketing, not from bank disclosure.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank annual reports surfaced digitalisation narratives and investment figures, but the search-result excerpts contained no supplier names.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale only partially: SK bank disclosures reliably reveal that transformation is happening and how much it costs, but who supplies it is more often revealed by vendor case studies and integrator reference pages. Collection design should pair both channels rather than relying on disclosures alone.

negative_findings.description: No investor presentation or capital-markets-day deck specific to a Slovak bank entity was located; only group-level presentations (KBC, RBI, Erste, Intesa) were found. Slovak banks are wholly owned and hold no local CMDs.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for SK-entity investor presentations returned press releases and annual reports instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The 'investor presentations' element of this cell's brief resolves to parent-group decks only; expectations and collection design should be adjusted accordingly.

coverage_gaps.description: Two SK-market banks disclose only through non-sk, non-en parent filings: UniCredit SK via Czech (výroční zpráva) and Italian group documents, mBank SK via Polish (raport roczny). The run's declared sk/en language scope cannot reach them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the language set to cs and pl for the branch-form banks, and it/de for group-level Intesa and Erste/RBI documents; add cs/pl glossary terms (výroční zpráva, oddział, sprawozdanie finansowe, raport roczny).

coverage_gaps.description: No outsourcing register was located. Under EBA outsourcing guidelines and DORA, banks must maintain a register of outsourcing/ICT third-party arrangements and report critical ones to the supervisor — the single highest-value vendor-naming artefact in this cell. It was not found in public form for any SK bank.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate whether NBS or the ECB publishes any aggregated DORA ICT third-party register extract, and whether SK banks reference their outsourcing register in Pillar 3 operational-risk chapters. If nothing is public, record it explicitly as a structurally closed channel rather than leaving it open.

coverage_gaps.description: Smaller and specialised SK banks in scope of the workstream were not covered in this pass: Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka (SZRB), Privatbanka, J&T Banka SK, Fio banka SK, Oberbank SK, Komerční banka SK branch, Wüstenrot/PSS and ČSOB stavebná sporiteľňa. PSS's výročná správa did surface incidentally.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a second pass over the NBS list of licensed banks and branches, and enumerate each entity's výročná správa page; smaller banks buy more from external vendors and disclose more concretely.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side and integrator-side reference libraries were only spot-checked (one PosAm reference, one Temenos story). This proved to be the channel that actually yields names, yet no systematic list of Slovak banking IT integrators was compiled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and crawl a roster of SK/CZ banking-IT integrator reference pages (PosAm, Soitron, Ness, Gratex, Asseco Central Europe, DXC, Accenture SK, Deloitte/EY SK) plus core/payments vendor customer-story libraries, filtered on Slovak bank names.

coverage_gaps.description: No URL in this slice was fetched and verified; all candidates come from search-result metadata. Several PDF URLs are long, deep-linked and version-suffixed (e.g. VÚB's '...AR_FS_VUB_2025_SK.pdf0', Prima banka's numeric preview-file ids) and are plausibly stale or malformed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Route every URL through the deterministic liveness pass; for PDF deep links prefer crawling the parent index page rather than persisting the deep link, since these banks rotate document paths yearly.

coverage_gaps.description: Disclosure cadence per bank was not established. Pillar 3 appears semi-annual at VÚB (period-coded filenames observed for 2024-06 and 2025-12) but the cadence for SLSP, Tatra banka, ČSOB, 365.bank and Prima banka is unconfirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Derive a per-bank collection calendar from the NBS banking disclosure measure and from observed filename period codes before scheduling recurring collection.

brief: Slovak systemic banks are wholly foreign-owned and privately procured, so their disclosure landscape splits cleanly in two: locally-hosted mandatory documents (výročné správy, ročné finančné správy and Pillar 3 'zverejňovanie informácií' under NBS Opatrenie č. 16/2014) on each bank's own site, and richer strategic detail in the parent groups' filings (Erste, RBI, KBC, Intesa Sanpaolo). Statutory registers — registeruz.sk, ORSR and the NBS CERI issuer repository, the last carrying structured ESEF filings — form the compliant fallback for entities such as UniCredit SK and mBank SK that publish nothing locally, and they also expose captive IT arms like Erste Digital's Slovak branch. The key finding of this pass is that the bank disclosures themselves reliably show that transformation is happening and what it costs, but rarely name suppliers; the two concrete vendor attributions obtained (Temenos payment hub and PosAm end-user-services outsourcing, both at Tatra banka) came from vendor and integrator reference libraries instead. Collection should therefore pair regulatory disclosure with systematic crawling of Slovak integrator reference pages, and must extend beyond sk/en into cs and pl to reach the branch-form banks.
